1	"""grokking_optimizers.compile — Targeted per-(optimizer, model, arch) build
2	with a portable AOT-then-JIT cache, YAML-driven search space, Bayesian
3	or Exhaustive autotune, optional PGO, and runtime-split AOT/JIT
4	subprocesses.
5	
6	This is the development-time companion to ``setup.py``. Where
7	``pip install -e .`` builds the full ``grokking_optimizers._ops``
8	extension with default flags, this module compiles a focused,
9	**maximally optimised** build for a single ``(optimizer, model, arch)``
10	triple. The pipeline is split into two halves so a CPU-only host can
11	do the heavy AOT compile and ship a cache file to the target GPU host,
12	which then does the JIT autotune sweep.
13	
14	Two-phase pipeline
15	==================
16	
17	**AOT phase (any host with the toolchain — no GPU required).**
18	
19	  1. Resolve sources for the chosen arch (bindings + every launcher +
20	     every model TU).
21	  2. Hash the source set, the host cflags, the device cflags, the
22	     resolved search-space, and the PGO state. Look up
23	     ``(optimizer, model, arch)`` in the cache. If all hashes match an
24	     entry with ``aot_completed_at != None`` and ``pgo_enabled`` agrees
25	     and the recorded artefact still exists → **cache hit**.
26	  3. Otherwise build with ``torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`` (ninja,
27	     ``MAX_JOBS=$(nproc)``, sccache wiring when on PATH), arch-tuned
28	     codegen + LTO + perf flags, and the ``SG_BUILD_*`` macros so
29	     headers can ``#if`` out unused specialisations.
30	  4. If ``--pgo`` is set, the AOT phase runs the 3-pass loop:
31	       instrument → workload → use. The PGO state is recorded so
32	       subsequent runs short-circuit when the workload hash matches.
33	  5. Record the artefact path, size, mtime, and SHA-256 in the cache.
34	     Mark ``aot_completed_at``. Save cache to disk.
35	
36	**JIT autotune phase (target GPU only).**
37	
38	  1. Load the resolved search space — by default, the COMPLETE programmatic
39	     space from build_full_search_space() (~billions of candidates per arch).
40	     Override with --search-space <path/to/your.yaml> to use a smaller
41	     curated space.
42	     Generate the cartesian product → apply static pre-filter rules →
43	     log the elimination count.
44	  2. Two autotune modes:
45	       - ``--mode exhaustive``: every survivor is built and timed.
46	         Cache is written every N trials so a Ctrl-C is recoverable.
47	       - ``--mode bayesian`` (default): Optuna TPE for ``--bayesian-trials``
48	         iterations + top-K refinement with ±2-step neighbours. The
49	         Optuna study persists to ``<cache_dir>/optuna_<opt>_<model>_<arch>.db``
50	         for cross-run resume.
51	  3. Timing is done by a **persistent subprocess worker** that holds a
52	     warm CUDA / HIP context for the full sweep, using CUDA-graph
53	     replay where the kernel supports it. Per-variant timeout falls
54	     back to one-shot subprocess timing on worker crash.
55	  4. Pick the winning combo (lowest median ms). Set ``cache.tuned_config``.
56	     Mark ``jit_completed_at``.
57	  5. Rewrite ``csrc/algorithms/tuned_configs.h`` with the winning
58	     macros so downstream consumers (setup.py builds, IDE Intellisense)
59	     pick up the tuned defaults.
60	  6. Rebuild the primary artefact with the tuned configs baked in.
61	
62	Runtime split
63	=============
64	``--runtime {aot, jit, both}`` controls which subprocesses run.
65	``both`` (default) spawns an AOT subprocess (CPU-only env) followed by
66	a JIT subprocess (GPU env). Each subprocess re-enters ``main`` with
67	the single-phase flag and reads/writes the same on-disk cache. This
68	means AOT and JIT can be tuned independently (env vars, library
69	versions, memory limits) without their settings bleeding into each
70	other. ``--aot-only`` / ``--jit-only`` remain as aliases.
71	
72	Cache schema v4
73	===============
74	The on-disk format is JSON; ``CACHE_VERSION == 4``. Forward-compatible
75	with v2 + v3 (auto-migrated on load). See ``INTERFACES.md`` for the
76	full shape. Headline additions over v2:
77	
78	    mode                 "exhaustive" | "bayesian" | None
79	    pgo_enabled          bool
80	    pgo_profile_dir      str | None
81	    pgo_workload_hash    str | None
82	    pgo_completed_at     str | None
83	    pgo_host             host dict
84	    search_space_hash    str (SHA-256 of resolved YAML space)
85	    bayesian_trials      [trial_record, …]   (stage="tpe" | "refine")
86	
87	Per-entry hashes (``source_hash``, ``host_cflags_hash``,
88	``device_cflags_hash``, ``search_space_hash``, plus ``pgo_enabled``)
89	all gate AOT freshness; any change invalidates the entry.
90	
91	Usage
92	=====
93	
94	CLI::
95	
96	    # End-to-end on a GPU host (AOT + Bayesian JIT autotune + profile)
97	    python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \\
98	        --optimizer supergrok2 --model mamba --arch sm_90 \\
99	        --cache build/.compile_cache.json \\
100	        --mode bayesian --bayesian-trials 500
101	
102	    # AOT-only on a CPU host with PGO (ships the cache)
103	    python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \\
104	        --optimizer supergrok2 --model mamba --arch sm_90 \\
105	        --cache build/.compile_cache.json --aot-only --pgo \\
106	        --pgo-workload scripts/pgo_workload.py --pgo-steps 1000 \\
107	        --aot-artifact-dir build/compiled/aot_artifacts
108	
109	    # JIT autotune only on the GPU host (consumes the cache)
110	    python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \\
111	        --optimizer supergrok2 --model mamba --arch sm_90 \\
112	        --cache build/.compile_cache.json --jit-only --mode exhaustive
113	
114	Importable::
115	
116	    from grokking_optimizers.compile import build, build_aot, build_jit, CompileCache
117	    cache = CompileCache(Path("build/.compile_cache.json"))
118	    so_path = build(optimizer="supergrok2", model="mamba", arch="sm_90",
119	                    cache=cache, autotune_mode="bayesian",
120	                    bayesian_trials=None,  # None = multi-criterion auto-stop

489	#
490	# For each CUDA arch we emit two -gencode flags:
491	#   1. compute_XX[a],code=sm_XX[a]  — SASS for the target SM
492	#   2. compute_XX,code=compute_XX   — PTX fallback so older drivers can JIT
493	#      forward to newer hardware that didn't exist at compile time.
494	# The "a" suffix on Hopper+ tells NVCC to emit arch-specific instructions
495	# (TMA, wgmma, tcgen05 etc.) that the non-"a" variant rejects.
496	
497	# SASS-only gencode toggle. When True, _nvcc_gencode_pair emits ONLY the
498	# ``code=sm_NN`` SASS gencode and DROPS the ``compute_NN`` PTX-fallback
499	# gencode. For an arch that ships a real kernel body (sm_90 / gfx942 today)
500	# this shrinks the fatbin and skips the JIT-from-PTX path entirely on the
501	# exact target SM. It is OFF by default because dropping the PTX fallback
502	# means the binary cannot JIT-forward onto a newer, not-yet-existing SM — so
503	# it's only safe when you are certain of the deployment GPU. Set via
504	# ``--sass-only`` on the CLI (wired in below) or by toggling this module flag.

508	def _nvcc_gencode_pair(num: int, suffix: str = "",
509	                       sass_only: Optional[bool] = None) -> List[str]:
510	    """Return the -gencode flags for a CUDA arch.
511	
512	    By default emits the SASS gencode + a ``compute_NN`` PTX-fallback gencode
513	    (so older drivers can JIT-forward onto newer hardware). When
514	    ``sass_only`` (defaulting to the module-level ``_SASS_ONLY_GENCODE``) is
515	    True, the PTX fallback is dropped — smaller fatbin / no JIT — which is
516	    only safe for archs whose exact SM is the known deployment target.
517	    """
518	    if sass_only is None:
519	        sass_only = _SASS_ONLY_GENCODE
520	    sm = f"sm_{num}{suffix}"
521	    compute = f"compute_{num}{suffix}"
522	    compute_fallback = f"compute_{num}"   # PTX fallback is always non-"a"
523	    flags = [f"-gencode=arch={compute},code={sm}"]
524	    if not sass_only:
525	        flags.append(
526	            f"-gencode=arch={compute_fallback},code={compute_fallback}")
527	    return flags

1207	#
1208	# Earlier revisions of this file embedded a hand-written YAML blob with a
1209	# small curated set of values per tuning dimension (e.g. block ∈ {64, 128,
1210	# 256, 512, 1024}). That biased the autotuner — Bayesian TPE could only
1211	# sample what we'd pre-decided was "reasonable". This was a mistake: the
1212	# whole point of an extensive optimization run is to discover non-obvious
1213	# winners, and pre-curating values defeats that.
1214	#
1215	# build_full_search_space() now generates the search space programmatically
1216	# from hardware specs:
1217	#   - every warp-aligned (sm_90) / wavefront-aligned (gfx942) block size
1218	#   - the full range of vector widths the load/store instructions support
1219	#   - every power-of-2 unroll factor up to a generous cap
1220	#   - every valid pipeline depth, register-budget, cluster shape, etc.
1221	#
1222	# The result is a Cartesian product of ~10⁹ candidates per arch — far too
1223	# many to materialize. Three consequences:
1224	#   1. ``cartesian()`` is now a generator (was a list).
1225	#   2. ``cartesian_count(space, arch)`` returns the size without iteration.
1226	#   3. ``ss_prefilter()`` accepts an iterable and streams survivors.
1227	# Bayesian TPE doesn't care about the size — it samples one config at a
1228	# time using the per-dim value lists. Exhaustive mode streams every survivor
1229	# via iter_prefilter (UNCAPPED — the full feasible space; see _run_exhaustive).
1230	#
1231	# Users can still override the entire space via --search-space <path.yaml>.

1249	# Live vs. dead tuning dimensions
1250	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1251	#
1252	# A producer→consumer audit of the emitted ``-DSG_TUNED_*`` macros against the
1253	# committed kernel bodies (grep of every *.cu / *.hip.cpp) showed that of the
1254	# ~22 macros the autotuner can emit, only FIVE are ever ``#ifdef``'d / read by
1255	# any kernel:
1256	#
1257	#   SG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE  (11 consumers)   — live
1258	#   SG_TUNED_VEC_WIDTH   (11 consumers)   — live
1259	#   SG_TUNED_UNROLL      (11 consumers)   — live
1260	#   SG_TUNED_ASYNC_DEPTH (12 consumers)   — live  (kernel clamps to [1,4])
1261	#   SG_TUNED_CLUSTER_SHAPE (2 consumers)  — live
1262	#
1263	# ``maxrregcount`` carries ``macro=None`` and is emitted as a real
1264	# ``--maxrregcount=N`` / ``-amdgpu-max-num-vgprs=N`` compiler flag, so it
1265	# genuinely changes the produced binary and is LIVE even though it is not an
1266	# SG_TUNED macro. All Pallas dims (kind == "pallas_kwarg") are real
1267	# ``pl.pallas_call`` arguments and are likewise LIVE.
1268	#
1269	# Every OTHER SG_TUNED_* / *_ENABLED macro (NUM_STAGES, SWIZZLE,
1270	# TMA_DESCRIPTORS, WGMMA_SHAPE, WARP_SPECIALIZATION, FP8/FP4_LAYOUT,
1271	# TCGEN05_VARIANT, LDS_PADDING, WAVES_PER_EU, MFMA_SHAPE, FP8/FP4_MFMA_LAYOUT,
1272	# SCHEDULER_HINT, WMMA_SHAPE, DPP_MODIFIER, TGSPLIT, the bare TMA bool) is
1273	# DEAD: no kernel reads it, so every distinct value produces a
1274	# binary-IDENTICAL artifact. Leaving these in the search space (a) inflates the
1275	# Cartesian product by ~10^4× on sm_90 / sm_100, wasting the sampler's trial
1276	# budget on binary-identical configs, and (b) poisons ``config_key`` so two
1277	# binary-identical configs hash to different keys → false cache misses → full
1278	# recompiles.
1279	#
1280	# We keep the macros *emittable* (the dims stay in the space, the
1281	# ``resolve_macros`` / ``resolve_extra_*_flags`` paths are untouched) so a dead
1282	# dim can be revived later by simply moving its name into ``_LIVE_TUNING_DIMS``.
1283	# But for now each dead dim is PINNED to a single default value (so it stops
1284	# expanding the search space) and DROPPED from ``config_key`` (so binary-
1285	# identical configs collapse to one cache entry).

1385	def _scan_kernel_ifndef() -> None:
1386	    """Scan the committed kernel trees ONCE for every ``#ifndef SG_TUNED_X``
1387	    guard AND the ``#define SG_TUNED_X <default>`` that immediately follows it,
1388	    populating both module caches (memoized; a cheap no-op once warm).
1389	
1390	    A tunable kernel wraps its default in::
1391	
1392	        #ifndef SG_TUNED_FOO
1393	        #define SG_TUNED_FOO <default>
1394	        #endif
1395	
1396	    so the autotuner can override the default with ``-DSG_TUNED_FOO=VAL``. We
1397	    record the guard token (so the search-space builder can AUTO-ADD a dim for a
1398	    newly-exposed knob with zero edits here) AND its in-source default (so an
1399	    auto-derived knob is PINNED to a byte-identical value rather than blindly
1400	    swept — a blanket sweep can violate a kernel ``static_assert``, e.g.
1401	    ``SG_TUNED_VIT_TILE_M`` has a single legal value). Pure ``//`` comment lines
1402	    are skipped so a commented-out guard doesn't inflate the space. Leaves both
1403	    caches empty-but-set when no source tree is visible (installed wheel).
1404	    """
1405	    global _KERNEL_IFNDEF_CACHE, _KERNEL_IFNDEF_DEFAULTS_CACHE
1406	    if _KERNEL_IFNDEF_CACHE is not None:
1407	        return
1408	    import re as _re
1409	    roots = [REPO_ROOT / "csrc", REPO_ROOT / "grokking_optimizers" / "kernels"]
1410	    # Anchored at line start (after optional whitespace): ``#ifndef SG_TUNED_X``.
1411	    ifndef_pat = _re.compile(r"^\s*#\s*ifndef\s+(SG_TUNED_[A-Z0-9_]+)")
1412	    # ``#define SG_TUNED_X <value...>`` — value is the remainder of the line.
1413	    define_pat = _re.compile(
1414	        r"^\s*#\s*define\s+(SG_TUNED_[A-Z0-9_]+)\s+(.+?)\s*$")
1415	    exts = {".cu", ".cuh", ".h", ".hpp", ".hip", ".cpp", ".cc", ".cxx"}
1416	    found: set = set()
1417	    defaults: Dict[str, str] = {}
1418	    for root in roots:
1419	        if not root.exists():
1420	            continue
1421	        for p in root.rglob("*"):
1422	            if p.suffix not in exts:
1423	                continue
1424	            try:
1425	                text = p.read_text(errors="ignore")
1426	            except OSError:
1427	                continue
1428	            lines = text.splitlines()
1429	            n = len(lines)
1430	            for i, line in enumerate(lines):
1431	                if line.lstrip().startswith("//"):
1432	                    continue  # comment-only line — not a live guard
1433	                m = ifndef_pat.match(line)
1434	                if not m:
1435	                    continue
1436	                macro = m.group(1)
1437	                found.add(macro)
1438	                # Look ahead a few lines for the matching ``#define`` default.
1439	                for j in range(i + 1, min(i + 4, n)):
1440	                    dm = define_pat.match(lines[j])
1441	                    if dm and dm.group(1) == macro:
1442	                        val = dm.group(2)
1443	                        for cmark in ("//", "/*"):  # strip a trailing comment
1444	                            k = val.find(cmark)
1445	                            if k != -1:
1446	                                val = val[:k].rstrip()
1447	                        if val and macro not in defaults:
1448	                            defaults[macro] = val
1449	                        break
1450	    _KERNEL_IFNDEF_CACHE = frozenset(found)
1451	    _KERNEL_IFNDEF_DEFAULTS_CACHE = defaults

1490	def _auto_derived_dims(dims: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
1491	    """Return a PINNED dim for every ``#ifndef SG_TUNED_*`` guard the kernels
1492	    expose that has NO explicit dim in ``dims``.
1493	
1494	    This is the self-configuring half of the search space: a kernel that adds a
1495	    new ``#ifndef SG_TUNED_FOO`` knob is DISCOVERED here with zero edits, so the
1496	    space always knows the kernels' full tuning surface (drift-proof) and every
1497	    knob is registered in ``config_key`` + emittable. Hand-written dims always
1498	    WIN — they're treated as overrides (richer value lists, custom
1499	    ``applies_to``/``kind``), so the explicit GEMM/tile/etc. specs in the per-arch
1500	    builders are unaffected.
1501	
1502	    An auto-derived knob is PINNED to its in-source ``#define`` default (a
1503	    single-value dim → ×1 in the Cartesian product, byte-identical canonical
1504	    build), NOT blindly swept. A blanket sweep is unsafe: many knobs carry a
1505	    compile-time ``static_assert`` (e.g. ``SG_TUNED_VIT_TILE_M`` has exactly one
1506	    legal value, 1088) or are sized constants (``pscan_block=512``) where an
1507	    arbitrary probe value would fail to compile or waste trial budget. PROMOTING
1508	    a discovered knob to an actually-swept dim is a deliberate, vetted act — add
1509	    an explicit ``_dim(name, ..., [hand-checked values], MACRO, ...)`` to the
1510	    relevant per-arch builder (it wins over this auto entry). A guard whose
1511	    default can't be read is left to its kernel ``#ifndef`` (discovery-only, no
1512	    dim added) so we never emit an unvetted ``-D`` value.
1513	    """
1514	    guarded = _kernel_ifndef_macros()
1515	    if not guarded:
1516	        return []
1517	    defaults = _kernel_ifndef_defaults()
1518	    extra: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
1519	    seen_names = {d.get("name") for d in dims}
1520	    for macro in sorted(guarded):
1521	        if _macro_has_explicit_dim(macro, dims):
1522	            continue
1523	        name = _macro_to_dim_name(macro)
1524	        if name in seen_names:
1525	            continue
1526	        raw = defaults.get(macro)
1527	        if raw is None:
1528	            continue  # discovery-only: no readable default → don't risk a value
1529	        try:
1530	            value: Any = int(raw, 0)  # decimal or 0x…
1531	            dtype = "int"
1532	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
1533	            value, dtype = raw, "enum"  # symbolic default (e.g. an enum token)
1534	        seen_names.add(name)
1535	        extra.append(_dim(name, dtype, [value], macro, ["device"]))

1549	    A dim is LIVE (not dead) when sweeping it actually changes the emitted
1550	    machine code; otherwise sweeping it just burns compiles on byte-identical
1551	    binaries. The determination is AUTO-DERIVED from the committed kernel
1552	    sources, so the search space tracks the kernels' real tuning surface no
1553	    matter what is being compiled (rather than a hand-maintained list that can
1554	    silently go stale when a kernel adds or drops an ``#ifdef SG_TUNED_*``):
1555	
1556	      * Pallas kwargs are arguments to ``pl.pallas_call`` — always live.

1558	        ``--maxrregcount=N``) always changes ptxas codegen — always live.

1560	        reads that macro (see :func:`_kernel_source_macros`). The hardcoded
1561	        ``_LIVE_TUNING_DIMS`` is only a defensive floor for the (degenerate)
1562	        case where the source scan finds nothing — e.g. a bodyless registry.
1563	    """
1564	    if spec.get("kind") == "pallas_kwarg":
1565	        return False
1566	    macro = spec.get("macro")
1567	    if macro is None:
1568	        return False  # real compiler flag (maxrregcount) — always affects code

1572	        # like SG_TUNED_CLUSTER_SHAPE_VOLUME for SG_TUNED_CLUSTER_SHAPE).
1573	        live = macro in detected or any(t.startswith(macro + "_")
1574	                                        for t in detected)
1575	        return not live
1576	    # Source scan empty (no kernel tree visible) — fall back to the floor set.
1577	    return spec.get("name") not in _LIVE_TUNING_DIMS

1862	        # maxrregcount tail) to keep prefilter-discriminating dims early in

1864	        _dim("opt_level", "int", [3, 2], None, ["device"]),
1865	        _dim("allow_expensive_opts", "bool", [False, True],
1866	             None, ["device"]),
1867	        _dim("vec", "int", vec_values,
1868	             "SG_TUNED_VEC_WIDTH", ["host", "device"]),
1869	        _dim("unroll", "int", unroll_values,
1870	             "SG_TUNED_UNROLL", ["host", "device"]),
1871	        # NOTE: num_stages is NOT a device dim — SG_TUNED_NUM_STAGES is dead on
1872	        # CUDA (no kernel #ifdef's it). It survives only as a LIVE pl.pallas_call
1873	        # kwarg in _build_pallas_space (and therefore stays in config_key + the
1874	        # cost-model column). ``stages_values`` is accepted for back-compat but
1875	        # only feeds the Pallas builder.
1876	        _dim("maxrregcount", "int", _maxrregcount_values(arch_key),
1877	             None, ["device"]),
1878	        _dim("swizzle", "int", [0, 32, 64, 128, 256],
1879	             "SG_TUNED_SWIZZLE", ["device"]),
1880	    ]
1881	
1882	    rules = list(_cuda_common_rules(arch_key))
1883	
1884	    if "tma" in features:
1885	        dims.append(_dim("tma_descriptors", "int", [0, 1, 2, 4, 8],

1890	                         list(range(1, _ASYNC_DEPTH_MAX + 1)),
1891	                         "SG_TUNED_ASYNC_DEPTH", ["device"]))
1892	
1893	    if "wgmma" in features:
1894	        # sm_90a: base wgmma shapes; sm_100a/103a add tcgen05 variants.
1895	        wgmma_shapes = ["m64n8k16", "m64n16k16", "m64n32k16",
1896	                        "m64n64k16", "m64n128k16", "m64n256k16"]
1897	        if "tcgen05" in features:
1898	            wgmma_shapes += ["m128n128k16_tcgen05", "m128n256k16_tcgen05",
1899	                             "m256n256k16_tcgen05"]
1900	        dims.append(_dim("wgmma_shape", "enum", wgmma_shapes,
1901	                         "SG_TUNED_WGMMA_SHAPE", ["device"]))
1902	        dims.append(_dim("warp_specialization", "int", [0, 1],
1903	                         "SG_TUNED_WARP_SPECIALIZATION", ["device"]))
1904	
1905	    if "cluster" in features:
1906	        if "tcgen05" in features:
1907	            cluster_shapes = _blackwell_cluster_shapes()
1908	            volume_cap = 16
1909	        else:
1910	            cluster_shapes = _hopper_cluster_shapes()
1911	            volume_cap = 8

1913	                         "SG_TUNED_CLUSTER_SHAPE", ["device"]))

1915	                      "expr": f"cluster_shape[0] * cluster_shape[1] * cluster_shape[2] <= {volume_cap}"})
1916

1918	        dims.append(_dim("fp8_layout", "enum", ["none", "e4m3", "e5m2"],
1919	                         "SG_TUNED_FP8_LAYOUT", ["device"]))
1920

1922	        dims.append(_dim("fp4_layout", "enum", ["none", "e2m1"],
1923	                         "SG_TUNED_FP4_LAYOUT", ["device"]))

1927	                         ["tma_a", "tma_b", "mma", "tma_mma"],

1930	    # NOTE: the L3-TC GEMM-mainloop knobs (dec/mb_gemm_stages,
1931	    # dec/mb/vit_gemm_interleave, pipe_depth) are DELIBERATELY NOT declared here.

2123	    """Hopper: tma + wgmma + cluster + fp8. Keep the original tight shape."""
2124	    arch_key = "sm_90a"
2125	    entry = ARCH_TABLE[arch_key]
2126	    return {
2127	        "dims": _pin_dead_dims([
2128	            _dim("block", "int", list(range(32, 1025, 32)),
2129	                 "SG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE", ["host", "device"]),
2130	            # --- ptxas optimizer knobs (bare compiler flags, macro=None) -----
2131	            # opt_level tunes ptxas's own PTX optimization (-Xptxas
2132	            # --opt-level=N); allow_expensive_opts toggles ptxas's expensive
2133	            # optimization passes. Both are LIVE — they change codegen directly
2134	            # — so _is_dead_dim keeps them swept (never pinned). Emitted by
2135	            # resolve_extra_nvcc_flags, matched on the dim name (like
2136	            # maxrregcount). Default value first so the canonical build matches
2137	            # the base flag list. Kept adjacent to the geometry head (before the
2138	            # high-cardinality maxrregcount/cluster_shape tail) so the Cartesian
2139	            # iteration still reaches vec>1 inside a small prefix window.
2140	            _dim("opt_level", "int", [3, 2], None, ["device"]),
2141	            _dim("allow_expensive_opts", "bool", [False, True],
2142	                 None, ["device"]),
2143	            _dim("vec", "int", [1, 2, 4, 8, 16],
2144	                 "SG_TUNED_VEC_WIDTH", ["host", "device"]),
2145	            _dim("unroll", "int", [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128],
2146	                 "SG_TUNED_UNROLL", ["host", "device"]),
2147	            # min_blocks => __launch_bounds__ 2nd arg (min CTAs/SM) on every
2148	            # sm_90 optimizer launcher (kernels/sm_90/*_sm90.cuh). Default 4
2149	            # matches the committed #ifndef SG_TUNED_MIN_BLOCKS literal, so the
2150	            # no-JSON build is byte-identical (verified via nvcc -E). LIVE on
2151	            # sm_90 (the scanner sees SG_TUNED_MIN_BLOCKS in the kernel bodies).
2152	            # MUST stay AFTER (block, vec, unroll): those three are the codegen
2153	            # template's baked operands (the SM_90A .j2 has no default() for them
2154	            # and the codegen self-tests sample dims[:3]); min_blocks is not a
2155	            # codegen dim, so it belongs past the first-three window.
2156	            _dim("min_blocks", "int", [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8],
2157	                 "SG_TUNED_MIN_BLOCKS", ["device"]),
2158	            # prod_regs / cons_regs => setmaxnreg targets for the producer /
2159	            # consumer warp-groups of the warp-specialized sm_90 paths (the
2160	            # fused megakernel's §3.4 split AND tile_pipeline.cuh share these
2161	            # tokens). First values 40 / 232 == the fused megakernel's in-header
2162	            # #ifndef defaults (SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS 40, SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS 232), so
2163	            # the untuned (no-JSON) build is byte-identical to the committed kernel.
2164	            # (Audit 2026-06-16 corrected a prior 32/200 first-value that did NOT
2165	            # match the kernel — verified vs csrc grep.) Multiples of 8 (setmaxnreg
2166	            # granularity); the producer wants few regs, the consumer holds the fp32
2167	            # accumulator + addressing. The scanner already sees both tokens
2168	            # (tile_pipeline.cuh) so they are LIVE; registering the dims sweeps them.
2169	            _dim("prod_regs", "int", [40, 24, 32, 48, 56],
2170	                 "SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS", ["device"]),
2171	            _dim("cons_regs", "int", [232, 168, 184, 200, 216, 240],
2172	                 "SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS", ["device"]),
2173	            # === RISKY (needs-parity) fused-megakernel launch dims ===========
2174	            # mega_block / grad_tile are consumed by the L3 fused megakernels
2175	            # (csrc/fused/sm_90/*: the fused tail + the decoder/vit/mamba drivers
2176	            # + the SuperGrok2 stage), tuned through the SAME sweep machinery via
2177	            # megakernel_cell_search_space (which builds this space). Defaults
2178	            # (256 / 1024) equal the prior literals so the untuned build is
2179	            # byte-identical (verified via nvcc -E). NEEDS-PARITY before shipping
2180	            # a non-default winner: mega_block must stay a multiple of the
2181	            # 128-thread warp-group (the §3.4 producer/consumer split) and
2182	            # grad_tile resizes a __shared__ array — the autotuner cannot prove
2183	            # either is correct; only the H100 parity gate can. Sweep sets are
2184	            # kept SMALL (2 values each) to respect the per-arch cardinality
2185	            # budget; widen once parity validates the shape.
2186	            _dim("mega_block", "int", [256, 512],
2187	                 "SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK", ["device"]),
2188	            _dim("grad_tile", "int", [1024, 2048],
2189	                 "SG_TUNED_GRAD_TILE", ["device"]),
2190	            # === L3-TC megakernel GEMM / tile dims (#12) =====================
2191	            # These are the REAL tile-tuning surface the autotuner was missing:
2192	            # the TC substrate headers (model_stage_{decoder,vit,mamba}_tc.cuh)
2193	            # size the wgmma fwd/bwd/dW GEMMs from them. Confirmed CONSUMED via a
2194	            # READ-ONLY grep of csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cuh (the kernel-builder owns
2195	            # those files; this only registers the dims that already exist):
2196	            #   SG_TUNED_TILE_M  — decoder (#ifndef 128, kSeq=4) + mamba
2197	            #                      (#ifndef 64, kSeq=8). Shared macro name.
2198	            #   SG_TUNED_TILE_N  — decoder + vit + mamba (#ifndef 128, shared).
2199	            #   SG_TUNED_{DEC,VIT,MB}_DW_SPLITK — per-model dW K-split factor
2200	            #                      (#ifndef 4 each; G==1 routes the single-CTA
2201	            #                      path). All three macros exist + are read.
2202	            # First value == the in-header #ifndef default, so the untuned
2203	            # (no-JSON) build is byte-identical (same convention as mega_block /
2204	            # grad_tile above). Kernel static_asserts: TILE_M multiple of 64
2205	            # (wgmma m64 atom) AND of kSeq (4/8 → every value below divides
2206	            # both); split-K >= 1. NEEDS-PARITY before a non-default winner
2207	            # ships (the autotuner cannot prove a resized __shared__ tile or a
2208	            # re-chunked dW reduce is correct — only the H100 gate can); sets
2209	            # are kept SMALL per the per-arch cardinality budget.

2211	            # DELIBERATELY OMITTED: a ViT TILE_M sweep. ViT uses a DISTINCT
2212	            # macro SG_TUNED_VIT_TILE_M whose static_assert requires a multiple
2213	            # of LCM(kSeq=17, 64)=1088 (a ViT sample is 17 rows); 64/128/256
2214	            # would all FAIL to compile, so it has exactly one legal value
2215	            # (1088) and is not a sweepable dim here. (model_stage_vit_tc.cuh
2216	            # reads SG_TUNED_TILE_N from the shared substrate, which IS swept.)
2217	            _dim("tile_m", "int", [128, 64, 256],
